name: Common Attack Pattern Enumeration and Classification
description: CAPEC is a community-developed list of common attack patterns — abstractions of techniques attackers use to exploit weaknesses (CWEs). Each CAPEC entry describes prerequisites, typical severity, attack flow, mitigations, and references to CWEs and CVE examples. Where CWE answers "what is the weakness?", CAPEC answers "how is the weakness attacked?". CAPEC is organized into views including Mechanisms of Attack and Domains of Attack.
relationToCloudSecurity: CAPEC patterns inform threat modeling and security testing for cloud applications. Patterns like CAPEC-21 (Exploitation of Trusted Identifiers), CAPEC-115 (Authentication Bypass), and the Injection/Probabilistic Techniques meta-patterns map directly to cloud-API-surface concerns. Tools that perform automated threat modeling often pivot through CAPEC.
relationToAISecurity: Historic CAPEC has limited direct AI coverage; AI-specific attack patterns are better served by MITRE ATLAS. Underlying CAPEC patterns (input validation, authentication, injection) still apply to AI service surfaces.

license.notes: CAPEC is governed by MITRE Terms of Use (free use with attribution). The XML schema and full content are downloadable from the MITRE CAPEC site.

lifecycle.notes: Corrected 2026-08-12: this entry previously described CAPEC as 'actively maintained though release cadence is slower than CWE/ATT&CK'. That understates it. capec_latest.xml reports Version="3.9" Date="2023-01-24", and the HTTP Last-Modified header agrees — no release in over three years. Treat CAPEC as a stable, effectively frozen reference rather than a moving target: mappings built on 3.9 are unlikely to be invalidated, but CAPEC will not reflect recent attack patterns, notably nothing AI/ML-specific from the last three years. active=true per the schema (3.9 is the version currently in force; nothing supersedes it).

current_extraction.notes: README-only stub pointing at MITRE CAPEC downloads. No local structured extraction yet.

extraction_history.reason: README pointer to upstream MITRE CAPEC

scope.upstream_caveat: CAPEC has no dedicated GitHub data repository — the weakest GitHub publication story among the MITRE frameworks in this tree, alongside FiGHT. The authoritative distribution is direct download from capec.mitre.org. A STIX rendering ships in mitre/cti under capec/2.0/ and capec/2.1/.
scope.release_pattern: No git tags or releases; versioned only by the Version and Date attributes on the XML root element. capec_latest.xml is an unversioned URL, so record Version/Date with any extraction.
scope.identifier_pattern: CAPEC-<n>, unpadded (CAPEC-1, CAPEC-100). Attack patterns, categories, and views share a single ID space, so a bare CAPEC-n does not indicate the object kind — check the containing element.

notes: Use CAPEC for attack-pattern threat modeling. Strongest when paired with CWE for the weakness side and ATT&CK for the adversary-behavior side. Because CAPEC is frozen at 3.9, it is a good candidate should a structured extraction ever be wanted — a one-time parse will not go stale quickly.

desired_end_state.notes: MITRE publishes the authoritative CAPEC catalog as XML/CSV downloads at capec.mitre.org/data/downloads.html. Per the no-bulk-mirror rule, this stays a stub pointing at upstream.
